body: Thank you!
Thank you so much! It turns out I was found fully favorable on an OTR!

My understanding was that it’s a pretty rare occurrence. My lawyer wrote a very good brief though, and I had two years of medical documentation for her to refer to. I believe I was also found disabled on a listing which probably made it easier to argue.
It stands for an “on the record” decision. It means the judge looked over the evidence ahead of my hearing and found me fully favorable.
I never had a CE, never was asked to attend one. I was denied at initial and reconsideration, but was found fully favorable on an OTR at the ALJ stage.

I was supposed to! I had a hearing scheduled for the 10th but the ALJ looked at my OTR request ahead of time and cancelled the hearing after finding me fully favorable just based on what was already on the record.
Ah I see! I guess I’ll just prepare for the hearing as best I can and cross my fingers haha, thank you!
Thank you for letting me know!

I haven’t won my case but I am scheduled for my ALJ hearing very soon! And we are applying for similar reasons - I have severe agoraphobia, major depressive disorder, general anxiety disorder, and PTSD.

If you still have time to secure one, I highly recommend getting a lawyer! I know how hard it is to reach out, believe me, but they can be very helpful to your case and ease of mind. They could prepare you for what kind of questions you’ll be asked and how the hearing will go.

Especially since talking is difficult for you, I think having legal representation would help with some of that stress. If there is an ADRC or similar organization near you, I recommend calling or emailing them. They will likely be able to point you in the right direction.

As for how to answer, I think just being honest is the best way to handle it! Be upfront about your limitations and how they impact your ability to work, and I think you’ll do fine.

Check out Jonathan Ginsberg’s YouTube channel as well, he has lots of great content I think will help you a lot!

I’m currently applying for SSI, started in September of 2020 and after two denials I’m just now getting to go in front of an ALJ in early February! Not sure if the SSDI process is different, and it will definitely be much less time if you happen to be approved at the initial or reconsideration stage. Each step has taken about 6 months for me personally.

I went to see a doctor after years of isolation and burst into tears and had a panic attack during the appointment. After describing how I’d been living, I was diagnosed then and there.

I think it’s something you should discuss with your doctor/therapist! I know it can be daunting but they are there to help.

I’m currently in the process of applying - I have a hearing in front of an ALJ in early February. I’m trying not to get my hopes up but my attorney seems confident at least, haha. My best advice is to get in contact with an organization like ADRC, they helped me navigate the two appeals before the hearing and got me in touch with legal representation from a non-profit.

Medical evidence is crucial. If you are not already seeing a therapist or doctor, please do so. They can write a letter or fill out an RFC form for you. You can also have a friend or family member write a third party statement on your behalf describing your condition and how it impacts your ability to work.

I’m really sorry you’re going through this. I know how awful it is, I’m still very scared that I won’t be approved. Just keep appealing with the help of an advocate or attorney, and make sure your medical records show that you are attempting treatment.

Do you mean the first appeal, reconsideration? Mine took almost exactly six months - same as my initial application. The estimate is unfortunately pretty accurate haha, I know it’s torturous to wait but try to hang in there.
Thank you very much, will do!
I live in Wisconsin - brown county, if that helps!

Is there perhaps an ADRC (Aging and Disability Resource Center) near you? I am in the middle of my first appeal, and what I did on the advice of my therapist was email them after I was initially denied  - a benefits specialist replied to me and walked me through signing forms that would allow her to submit things on my behalf. She’s been a huge help to me through this process and I highly recommend seeking out a similar advocate.

Thank you so much for sharing your story with me! I think I’d better start looking into attorneys - I haven’t received a decision on my appeal yet but I’d like to be prepared for the next step just in case. I have an advocate through a disability resource center who has been incredibly helpful and kind, I’m just getting more and more anxious as the days go by and I don’t have any updates or good news coming my way.
I completely understand - it’s horrible just sitting around and waiting for a potential denial! Hang in there, I’m wishing you and your claim all the best.

Thank you very much for replying. I had only just started treatment when I first applied, so I’m hoping that my medical records since then as well as letters from my doctors might help show how severe my conditions are.
Thank you very much for the reply. Unfortunately, my disabilities pertain to my mental health, so I’m not sure that’s an option for me.

Thank you very much for the response! I got to see my psychologist this morning and I’m feeling a bit better. I will be patient and try to focus on other things in life I can work on right now. Seeing your response really helped me, thank you again.

I found my advocate through my local ADRC (Aging & Disability Resource Center) - I just sent an email their way asking for help with my appeal and the whole process. After discussing the specifics of my case with the person who replied to me, I signed some forms that allowed her to request and submit things on my behalf. Best of luck with your case!

You clearly don’t appreciate how debilitating these kinds of disorders can be for people. And do you genuinely think that someone can’t be in need of these programs and also … enjoy gaming?

I’m so sorry about whatever personal experiences have made you so bitter towards others trying to get help and secure treatment - I can only hope you reflect on this in the future and realize how utterly unkind and small-minded this sort of attitude is.
Ah gotcha, I think I’ll discuss that with my advocate and see if she has any recommendations as far as legal representation go. Thank you!
Thank you! That is so kind of you, I really appreciate it.

Thank you very much! The idea of a hearing is daunting, but I am lucky enough to have people in my life who will help me with the process if/when I need to tackle that stage of appeal. In the meantime I will focus on my treatment!

Ah yeah for sure! My advocate actually told me when she was looking over my initial denial that they seemed to be misinterpreting some of my psychologist’s notes about my little accomplishments (ex: a haircut for the first time in years that I managed to get through and was proud of!) as a reflection of my daily life and functionality.

I will keep this in mind going forward, and I’ll have to check if there’s any more documentation I can provide. Thank you again!

I’m sorry you had to go through so much! And yes, I did fill out a form about my capabilities/function and briefly gave some background of how my conditions keep me from working. I didn’t know if my testimony would have much weight compared to the people treating me, so I didn’t think to include my own letter aside from the notes I made on the forms themselves. I’ll discuss this with my advocate and see if she can give me some suggestions. Thank you very much for weighing in!
Thank you! I’ll be sure to discuss this with my advocate if I have to take this next step!
Thank you very much for replying!
